question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we rewrite the integral as

$$
\int (4y-1)^{-1/2}\,\text{d}y.
$$

Now, we let $u=4y-1.$ Then differentiating with respect to $y$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}y}=4\,⟹\,\text{d}y=\frac{1}{4}\text{d}u.
$$

We now write our integral in terms of $u,$ calculate the integral as normal, and write the final answer in terms of $y$ at the very end:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (4y-1)^{-1/2}\,\text{d}y & =\int {u}^{-1/2}\cdot \frac{1}{4}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\int {u}^{-1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{1}{(1/2)}{u}^{1/2}+C \\  & =\frac{2}{4}\cdot {u}^{1/2}+C \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(4y-1)^{1/2}+C \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{4y-1}}{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let's double-check that our result is correct. If we differentiate the result, then it should come out to the original integrand:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}[\frac{\sqrt{4y-1}}{2}+C] & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}[\sqrt{4y-1}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(C) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}[(4y-1)^{1/2}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(C) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{1}{2}(4y-1)^{-1/2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}y}(4y-1)+0 \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(4y-1)^{-1/2}\cdot 4 \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{4y-1}}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

\int (3-4x)^{2/3}\,\text{d}x.

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-4\,⟹\,\text{d}x=-\frac{1}{4}\text{d}u.
$$

We now write our integral in terms of $u,$ calculate the integral as normal, and write the final answer in terms of $x$ at the very end:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (3-4x)^{2/3}\,\text{d}x & =\int {u}^{2/3}\cdot (-\frac{1}{4})\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}\int {u}^{2/3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{1}{5/3}{u}^{5/3}+C \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{3}{5}{u}^{5/3}+C \\  & =-\frac{3}{20}{u}^{5/3}+C \\  & =-\frac{3}{20}(3-4x)^{5/3}+C \\  & =-\frac{3}{20}\sqrt[3]{(3-4x)^{5}}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let's double-check that our result is correct. If we differentiate the result, then it should come out to the original integrand:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[-\frac{3}{20}(3-4x)^{5/3}+C] & =-\frac{3}{20}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[(3-4x)^{5/3}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) \\  & =-\frac{3}{20}\cdot \frac{5}{3}(3-4x)^{2/3}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3-4x)+0 \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}(3-4x)^{2/3}\cdot (-4) \\  & =(3-4x)^{2/3} \\  & =\sqrt[3]{(3-4x)^{2}}\,✓\end{aligned}
